purpose: Turn one meeting's synthetic notes into a reviewed action-item list: a writer drafts it, a critic checks it against the rulebook, the approver decides at one gate.

agents.name: action-writer
agents.purpose: Draft the action-item list from one meeting's notes.
instructions: Read the meeting notes and list every commitment made in the meeting exactly once: something a person or the group agreed will be done.

Ideas, suggestions nobody took up, declined offers, open questions, decisions with nothing to do, plans that depend on an unknown outcome, agreeing to discuss or decide something later, items already done and repeats of a commitment already listed are not actions.
action starts with a verb. owner is the attendee who committed; if nobody did, 'unassigned'.

due is an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the notes give a date; resolve a relative date ('by Friday') against the meeting date. When the notes give a deadline that cannot be resolved to a date, copy its words exactly. If the notes give no deadline, 'not stated'. Never guess either field.
source is the one sentence the action came from, copied exactly, at most 25 words.
When revising, fix every finding you are given and change nothing else.

agents.name: action-critic
agents.purpose: Check the action-item list against the notes and the rulebook.
instructions: You receive the meeting notes, the action-item list and the rulebook. Check every row and every commitment in the notes against every rule.
A finding's location is the row ID (A1, A2, ...); for a missed commitment, quote the words from the notes it comes from.
Apply each rule's severity exactly as the rulebook gives it. The verdict is fail when there is any blocker or major finding.

gates.decision: Approve or reject the reviewed action-item list before it is final.

rulebook.name: action-rules

rules.rule: Every action is backed by a quoted sentence from the notes; nothing invented.
Owner and due date come only from the notes; if missing, say 'unassigned' or 'not stated', never guess.
No duplicates and nothing missed: every commitment in the notes appears exactly once.

definitions: A commitment is a person or the group agreeing to do something; plans that depend on an unknown outcome are not actions.
Agreeing to discuss or decide something later is not an action.

A due date is an ISO date when the notes give a date (a relative date such as 'by Friday' is resolved against the meeting date), the deadline's words copied exactly from the notes when they cannot be resolved to a date, or 'not stated' when the notes give no deadline; never a guessed date.
